title: Fasil Ghebbi, Gondar
summary: Fasil Ghebbi is the fortified royal compound at Gondar, Ethiopia, enclosed by a wall about 900 metres long and holding palaces, churches and other buildings. Emperor Fasilides made Gondar a permanent capital in 1636, and work on his castle began in the late 1630s. Gondar remained the capital until its decline in the late 18th century.

uncertainty.note: Start is 1636, when Fasilides established Gondar as permanent capital; the castle itself began in the late 1630s. End is the "late 18th century" decline of the capital given by Zamani; a second page dates later events (sack 1888, Addis Ababa founded 1892) so the end is approximate.
